title: A group document named by a policy is served to that policy's audience regardless of the group's own read grants, under four bounding rules
content:
A replica must fold a group's membership to evaluate a policy that names it, so the same reasoning that makes the `auth` and `document` scopes always readable extends to rosters: a group named by a grant is served to any subject the naming document's policy serves, **regardless of the group's own read grants**. The `scoped-reads` recipe shows Carol reading the reviewers roster she is not on, past the roster's Alice-only policy, because a replica must fold that membership to evaluate the report's grants — while Mallory, whom the report serves nothing, does not, and below `authGroups` nobody does. Naming a group publishes its roster to that audience; a document whose access list must stay confidential cannot have a replicated policy at all.

Four rules bound the exemption (`getGroupReferencers` on the operation index is the lookup):

- **Only the member list is served.** A group's other scopes stay behind its own grants, because the member list is the only thing the audience must fold.
- **Only a referencing document's *domain* scopes decide its audience.** Every holder reads a document's `auth` and `document` scopes, so testing those would serve every referenced group to everybody.
- **One level.** A referencer that is itself a group is skipped, and a referencer's own readability comes from its policy alone, so a reference cycle terminates. Cycles are reachable even though the reducer forbids a group naming a group: the reference relation is recorded from an operation's *input*, including an operation later stored denied, so a refused grant leaves a row behind that validation never saw.
- **At most a hundred referencers are examined.** Each costs a model build and the relation is append-only, so an unbounded scan would make a widely-named group permanently expensive to read. Past the bound the group is withheld — the direction that fails closed — and the truncation is logged.
